RR 1.105 (1.049 to 1.163), 95% interval

clinical cure at test-of-cure. random-effects, estimator REML, k = 3.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 0.6562 on 2 df

The analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00509106 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate for Ceftaroline Compared to That for Ceftriaxone at the Test of Cure (TOC) in the Modified ' (population: Mitte); NCT00621504 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate at Test-of-Cure (TOC) in the Modified Intent-to-Treat Efficacy (mitte) Populations' (population: Mitte); NCT01371838 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate for Ceftaroline Compared to That for Ceftriaxone at Test of Cure (TOC) in CE Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and mitte.

A clinically evaluable population excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are selected subsets of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield higher cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population.

Not that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.

This screen found no published synthesis pooling these three trials. The nearest relevant record is a network meta-analysis across many community-acquired pneumonia regimens (PMID 34540732), which answers a different question from a ceftaroline-versus-ceftriaxone pool. 42 records matched, 42 read, 18 flagged by title, one appraised; the rest were not read, so absence here is absence from this screen and not from the literature.

Two contributing trials register the primary in the mitte population and one in the CE population. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so this ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. GRADE indirectness is downgraded for it.

Unlike tigecycline, ceftaroline's result holds under adjustment: the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, and it still excludes no difference. Recorded because the two topics separate on exactly this.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 4. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML1.1048 (1.0494 to 1.1633)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 2 degree(s) of freedom (t = 4.3027)1.1048 (0.9868 to 1.2371)

The published point is 1.1049 and the house-rule point is 1.1048. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

Abstract

Question. In Ceftaroline fosamil versus ceftriaxone in bacterial pneumonia, what is the effect on versus intravenous ceftriaxone on clinical cure at test-of-cure?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Clinical cure at test-of-cure: risk ratio 1.1 (1.05 to 1.16) across 3 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed closely (I-squared 0%); and certainty of the evidence was low.3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In Ceftaroline fosamil versus ceftriaxone in bacterial pneumonia, what is the effect on versus intravenous ceftriaxone on clinical cure at test-of-cure? It pools 3 randomised trials, against intravenous ceftriaxone. The outcome pooled is clinical cure at test-of-cure. Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. Registry throughout. Every count and denominator read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 3 randomised trials (NCT00509106, NCT00621504, NCT01371838), pooled here at 1.105 (95% CI 1.049 to 1.163) for clinical cure at test-of-cure. Certainty in that estimate is rated LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. What this estimate does not establish is recorded in full with the result in Results, and is not restated here. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] A search for published syntheses matched 42 record(s); 42 were read and 1 appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is Comparing Several Treatments with Antibiotics for Community-Acquired Pneumonia: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis ((indexed 2021; journal not extracted), 2021). Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — synthesis

For clinical cure at test-of-cure, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 3 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP; these are randomised trials starting HIGH. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Results

The pooled risk ratio for clinical cure at test-of-cure was 1.1 (1.05 to 1.16) across 3 trials, against intravenous ceftriaxone.1

Noted on this pool. This screen found no published synthesis pooling these three trials. The nearest relevant record is a network meta-analysis across many community-acquired pneumonia regimens (PMID 34540732), which answers a different question from a ceftaroline-versus-ceftriaxone pool. 42 records matched, 42 read, 18 flagged by title, one appraised; the rest were not read, so absence here is absence from this screen and not from the literature. The analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. The populations pooled are CE and mitte. Two contributing trials register the primary in the mitte population and one in the CE population. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so this ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. GRADE indirectness is downgraded for it. A clinically evaluable population excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are selected subsets of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield higher cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population. Unlike tigecycline, ceftaroline's result holds under adjustment: the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, and it still excludes no difference. Recorded because the two topics separate on exactly this. Not that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.656, on degrees of freedom 2.3

What this does not establish: Not that any trial is free of bias -- no risk-of-bias assessment is recorded, and a pooled estimate without one is arithmetic, not a graded finding. Not superiority: these are non-inferiority trials against an active comparator, and a risk ratio near 1 is the expected result of a successful one rather than evidence of equivalence. Not anything about the fourth seeded trial, which is excluded above. Not agreement with any published synthesis; none has been read.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family)4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py, which assembles the prompt from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and refuses to send it if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. It was given this project's NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule so the comparison measures judgement rather than house dialect.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 12 of 18 judgements -- 66.7%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 3 of 3 disagree, D2 0 of 3 disagree, D3 0 of 3 disagree, D4 3 of 3 disagree, D5 3 of 3 disagree and overall 3 of 3 disagree.7

That rate was measured before this review's D1 judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.8

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 9 of 18 judgements -- 50.0%. By domain: D1 0 of 3 disagree, D2 0 of 3 disagree, D3 0 of 3 disagree, D4 3 of 3 disagree, D5 3 of 3 disagree and overall 3 of 3 disagree.9

3 D1 judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any D1 disagreement that remains is one where this assessment said SOME_CONCERNS rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said NO_INFORMATION there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to SOME_CONCERNS. So a claim that 'the D1 disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.10

D1 now agrees with assessor 2 on every compared result.11

Class 94 records assessor 2 saying NO_INFORMATION on D1/D2/D3 `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are D1=SOME_CONCERNS on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.12

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP; these are randomised trials starting HIGH.2

LOW certainty. Downgraded once for non-uniform masking with two unjudgeable domains, and once because the pool combines results defined in different analysis populations. Not downgraded for inconsistency or imprecision, neither of which the fit supports.3

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D4 on 3 result(s), D5 on 3 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step5
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
clinical cure at test-of-cureLOW3HIGHrisk of bias -- All three results are SOME_CONCERNS: non-uniform masking (one trial's care provider unmasked) on an assessed cure endpoint, with D2 and D3 NO_INFORMATION. (move: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s)); inconsistency -- The stored refit gives tau^2 exactly zero, Q 0.6553 on 2 df, p = 0.7206, I-squared 0.00%. The three trials agree. (move: no downgrade); indirectness -- the pool crosses an analysis-population boundary: two trials register the primary in mitte and one in CE. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so the pooled ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. (move: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s)); imprecision -- k = 3 and the effect is consistent. The Hartung-Knapp interval, 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, still excludes no difference, so the conclusion survives the small-k adjustment. (move: no downgrade); publication bias -- k = 3; asymmetry tests have no power (Handbook 13.3.5.4). (move: Not assessable -- no rating applied)

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled RR is 1.105 (95% CI 1.049 to 1.163) over 3 trials, against intravenous ceftriaxone. Certainty is rated LOW. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 3 trials, I-squared is 0%; tau-squared 0; 1 of the 3 trial intervals include no effect and 2 exclude it. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 1.105 (95% CI 1.049 to 1.163) over 3 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled not established -- the outcome list was not read. Which trials that synthesis carries: Not read. Only the title and the opening of the abstract were seen; the included-study list was not. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 3 trials, assessed for risk of bias as SOME_CONCERNS on 3 result(s). GRADE certainty is LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 3 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18; All four seeded registrations read on 2026-08-18; three pooled, one excluded on the grounds stated in the analysis block. Published syntheses. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (ceftaroline[tiab]) and (pneumonia[tiab] or cabp[tiab] or cap[tiab]) and (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR "pooled"[tiab] or focus[tiab]). It matched 42 record(s), of which 42 were retrieved and 42 read; 1 appraised. Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.5

[Draft] Certainty was rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-21. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/ceftaroline-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. This screen found no published synthesis pooling these three trials. The nearest relevant record is a network meta-analysis across many community-acquired pneumonia regimens (PMID 34540732), which answers a different question from a ceftaroline-versus-ceftriaxone pool. 42 records matched, 42 read, 18 flagged by title, one appraised; the rest were not read, so absence here is absence from this screen and not from the literature. Two contributing trials register the primary in the mitte population and one in the CE population. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so this ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. GRADE indirectness is downgraded for it. Unlike tigecycline, ceftaroline's result holds under adjustment: the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, and it still excludes no difference. Recorded because the two topics separate on exactly this.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Not read. Only the title and the opening of the abstract were seen; the included-study list was not.4

Conclusions

[Draft] Across 3 randomised trials, RR was 1.105 (95% CI 1.049 to 1.163) for clinical cure at test-of-cure against intravenous ceftriaxone. Certainty in that estimate is LOW. That is the estimate. What the evidence shows -- stated as a finding rather than as a number -- is the author's sentence.1

[Draft] What a clinician should do differently on this evidence -- the estimate and certainty stated above -- is a recommendation, not a measurement. No field on this object can back one, and none is drafted. It is the author's sentence.2
